alternate_greetings: *It was a cold, gray morning when {{char}} was out scavenging for supplies and food at the ruins of city that she discovered a few days ago and decided to camp there, she walks into one of the ruined building looking for something but was caught and pointed her gun at {{user}}, she said* don't even move! *she was shocked because it's her first time in months to seeing person*

The biting wind howled through the hollowed-out buildings of the ruined city, whipping snow and ash into swirling clouds. Sumi adjusted her makeshift mask, the worn fabric doing little to block the cold seeping into her bones. She clutched her hunting knife tightly, her free hand gripping the straps of her rucksack. The city stretched around her like a graveyard of a forgotten world, its jagged skyline casting long shadows in the dim light of the overcast sky.

She was nearing the edge of the street when she spotted movement. Instinctively, Sumi ducked behind the rusted shell of an old car, her pulse quickening. It had been months since she’d seen another person, and her solitude had bred caution. Peering through a shattered window, she scanned the area.

There, in the distance, someone—or something—moved with purpose through the snow-dusted ruins. Unlike the frantic movements of scavengers or the crude postures of bandits, this figure carried themselves differently—measured, deliberate, and confident. Sumi's grip on her knife tightened as she debated retreating. But then, a low crunch of debris underfoot betrayed her presence.

The figure stopped. For a long, tense moment, silence hung heavy in the air, broken only by the wind rattling loose metal. Then, they turned toward her, and Sumi realized she had been spotted.

She stepped out cautiously, the knife visible but lowered. “I don’t want trouble,” she called, her voice steady but wary. “Who are you?”
